clue.text: A bogus journalist feeling guilty

blocks.note: taken as written
a sham is something bogus, a fake
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A fraudulent reporter is wracked with guilt over invented stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ashamed is to be overcome by remorse or embarrassment about something one has done wrong.

clue.text: Crossing in America turning up in Germany

definitions.note: a prepositional phrase defining a place name, fair because the clue asks for somewhere that is located in Germany, and Spandau is such a place

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up makes the letters read from bottom to top
the first word goes in, inside the next one

blocks.note: a panda crossing was a type of British pedestrian crossing
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A road crossing in the USA that somehow reappears in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: A panda crossing was a short-lived British pedestrian crossing of the 1960s, a cousin of the zebra crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Spandau is a district of Berlin, famous for its prison where Nazi war criminals were held, so it lies in Germany.

clue.text: Trelawney's somewhat taken aback by warning

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the word is used, a run of its letters
taken aback is read literally as taken backwards, against the reading direction

blocks.note: the opening run of letters in the name

explanation.surface: Someone called Trelawney is a little startled by a warning he has been given.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a signal that warns of danger, so the two words are synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Concerto offers more per performance

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A concert hall offering a bigger fee each time a work is played.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's fifth piano concerto is universally known by its nickname, so the name stands for that piece of music.

clue.text: People turn valleys into hills

blocks.note: men are people
dips are hollows or small valleys in the ground

explanation.surface: A fanciful picture of people reshaping the landscape, filling valleys up into hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mendips, or Mendip Hills, are a range of limestone hills in Somerset, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mendips is the everyday name for a particular English upland range, so it is a specific example of hills.

clue.text: Where one may regret turning up to work, having to start early

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up makes the letters read from bottom to top
the start of a word is only its opening letter

blocks.note: to rue something is to regret it
op. is short for opus, a musical work
the opening letter of early

explanation.surface: A grumble about the commute, regretting an early start at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Where' alone is the definition: a place one might be; the rest is all wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe is a continent, a place, which answers the question 'where' in the loose crossword sense of a location.

clue.text: Tyranny makes its mark in religion

indicators.note: the mark is placed in, inside the faith word

blocks.note: a spot is a mark or blemish
deism is belief in a creator god based on reason

explanation.surface: Oppressive rule that leaves its stamp on a nation's faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Despotism is government by a single ruler with absolute power, the same oppressive rule as tyranny.

clue.text: It's coarse to be nosy without a show of modesty

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: to pry is to be nosy, to snoop
rude means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: A prim remark that it is vulgar to poke into others' business without some decorum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' reads as lacking, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudery is excessive concern with propriety, an outward display of being easily shocked by indecency.

clue.text: Such a one may need concerted pain treatment

definitions.text: Such a one may need concerted pain treatment

indicators.note: treatment means the words are worked on and processed into a different form

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps getting hurt may need a concentrated course of pain relief.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a person forever having mishaps often needs medical help for pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone accident-prone keeps suffering mishaps and injuries, so such a person often needs treatment.

clue.text: Beware of grot

blocks.note: first meaning: the Latin warning cry once used by schoolboys to signal a teacher approaching
second meaning: a grot is a poetic word for a grotto, an underground hollow

explanation.surface: A warning to steer clear of grot, which in British slang means dirt or rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grot' looks like British slang for grime, but here it is the literary short form of grotto.
explanation.definitionFit: Cave is Latin for 'look out', used as a warning in English school slang, and a cave is a natural hollow in rock.

clue.text: Characteristic of a rogue, taking umbrage over responsibilities

indicators.note: one word taking another holds it inside itself, wrapped around it

blocks.note: pique is resentment or offence, which is what taking umbrage means
cares are worries or charges one is responsible for

explanation.surface: A roguish type who sulks and takes offence when burdened with duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Picaresque fiction follows the adventures of a likeable scoundrel, so the adjective describes things typical of such a rascal.

clue.text: On paper, one should have some influence

definitions.text: On paper, one should have some influence

blocks.clueFragment: On paper, one should have some influence
blocks.note: surface reading: in theory, someone ought to carry some weight
setter's reading: on a newspaper, the person in charge of content certainly has influence

explanation.walkthrough: 'On paper' means 'in theory' in the surface, but cryptically it means working on a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who runs a newspaper decides what is printed, and so wields real influence over its readers.

clue.text: One makes better vehicle to follow outdated model

indicators.note: the vehicle is placed to come after the model, so the second piece sits on the end

blocks.note: the Hillman Imp was a small British car made in the 1960s and 70s, long out of production
Rover is a British make of car, and a rover is also a roaming vehicle

explanation.surface: A car buff upgrading from an old model to a newer vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hillman Imp was a British car of the 1960s and 70s; Rover is another British car make.
explanation.definitionFit: An improver is literally someone or something that brings about improvement, making things better than before.

clue.text: Backer of the right in corrupt purpose

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoilt and twisted out of its proper form
one piece goes in, inside the other, rather than beside it

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram material
Rt is the standard abbreviation for right, as in Rt Hon

explanation.surface: A political backer of the right wing whose aims have been corrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backer of the right' looks like a single political phrase, but the definition stops at Backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A backer and a supporter are both people who give help, money or encouragement to a cause or person.

clue.text: Dolly bird installed in temple of Athene

indicators.note: something installed is put in place inside something else

blocks.note: Dolly Parton is the American country singer
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: An attractive young woman given a place in a Greek goddess's shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dolly bird' is old British slang for a pretty young woman, but the words split: Dolly is the singer, bird is a hen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon on the Athenian Acropolis was built as a sanctuary dedicated to Athena, patron goddess of the city.

clue.text: Party always backed by the state

indicators.note: backed means put into reverse, so the word for always runs back to front

blocks.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party
ay (or aye) is an old word for always, ever

explanation.surface: A political party that is forever supported by the state.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya is a North African country, so it is an example of a sovereign nation, the sense of state here.

clue.text: Priest having billet with soldiers

indicators.note: with puts one piece alongside the next, joining them end to end

blocks.note: a pad is slang for a place to sleep, as a billet is a soldier's lodging
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army

explanation.surface: An army chaplain lodging alongside the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a common crossword source of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the informal name for a military chaplain, a clergyman serving with the armed forces.

clue.text: A bribe given to 12 was effective

blocks.note: taken as written
a vail is an archaic word for a tip or gratuity, a sweetener
the answer to 12 across is editor, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: Slipping a backhander to a newspaper chief did the trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 12 across, whose answer is commonly shortened to ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Availed means was of use or helped, which is to say it worked or had the desired effect.

clue.text: Partner going off creates deadlock

blocks.note: food going off is becoming stale
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: A spouse walking out leaves a marriage at an impasse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going off' reads as leaving, but it means turning bad, like food.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a stalemate leaves neither side able to win, so the word is used for any situation where no progress is possible.

clue.text: Nearly broke, but pinching a cent is an offence

indicators.note: broke is read as broken apart, so the letters are smashed and reassembled
pinching means grabbing and holding something within

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram material
c is the abbreviation for cent

explanation.surface: Someone almost penniless, yet stealing even a single cent is still a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly broke' reads as almost bankrupt, but Nearly is the fodder and broke the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for theft, the unlawful taking of another's property, which is a crime.

clue.text: Gordius is lean without something to give nourishment

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: lean means thin
the setter Gordius, speaking of himself, says I am

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to being skinny for lack of food.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name; Gordius is the setter of this puzzle, so his name stands for I or ME, here I AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Thiamin is vitamin B1, a nutrient the body needs from food, so it is a substance that nourishes.

clue.text: They are drawn whoever wins

blocks.note: surface reading: a paradox of a match ending drawn even though someone wins
setter's reading: in cricket the wooden posts are pulled out of the ground when play ends, whatever the result

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' suggests a tied game; in cricket, the posts of the wicket are drawn, pulled up, at the close of play.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumps are the three upright posts of a cricket wicket, removed at the close of every day's play regardless of the result.

clue.text: Provide article used in urology

indicators.note: something used in another thing is put inside it

blocks.note: to cater is to provide food or what is needed
the definite article

explanation.surface: A supply request for a piece of urological equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the answer is an article used in urology.
explanation.definitionFit: A catheter is a thin tube inserted into the bladder to drain urine, a standard tool of the urinary specialist.

clue.text: Inexperienced type that's after a bird

indicators.note: after places the first-named piece behind the second, at the end

blocks.note: a rook is a black bird of the crow family
i.e., id est, means 'that is'

explanation.surface: A novice birdwatcher chasing a particular bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a raw recruit or newcomer, someone new to a job or sport who lacks experience.

clue.text: Function of police in Omagh or Derry?

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the following words, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: a run of letters across the middle of these words

explanation.surface: A question about policing in Northern Ireland, naming two of its towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Omagh and Derry are towns in Northern Ireland, where policing has been a fraught issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping law and order is the stated purpose of a police force, so order is what police maintain.

clue.text: Canteen's last gamble can break the mould

indicators.note: last asks for only the final letter of the word before it
to break the words is to smash them up and rebuild them in another order

blocks.note: the final letter of canteen
taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A works canteen takes a daring risk that breaks with convention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break the mould' looks like an idiom for innovating, but the mould is the pudding, and 'can' is fodder rather than a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A blancmange is a set milk pudding turned out of a mould, so it can be called 'the mould', as the British once called it 'a shape'.

clue.text: A couple of notes for a white elephant

blocks.note: do and me (or mi) are the first two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A small payment in banknotes for a useless, costly possession.
explanation.walkthrough: This dates from 2002, when London's Millennium Dome stood empty and was widely mocked as a costly white elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A white elephant is a showy, expensive thing nobody can use; the Millennium Dome was notoriously labelled one after the year 2000.

clue.text: Prime property, apart from 2

blocks.note: surface reading: an estate agent's top-quality house or land
setter's reading: a feature that every prime number shares, except the number two

explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime property' sounds like real estate, but it means a mathematical attribute of prime numbers; every prime except two is not divisible by two.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of not being divisible by two is shared by all primes except the first one, the only even prime.

clue.text: Its issue is other than dry

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Something whose output is anything but dry.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: what comes out of the answer is water, the very opposite of dry.
